extracted.intended_audience: artists, critics, and educated readers interested in aesthetics and the moral/social purpose of art
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating and producing art that genuinely unites people and serves as a moral/spiritual organ of human life rather than as an amusement, counterfeit, or exclusive luxury. Emphasises transmission of feeling, accessibility, moral aim, and authentic origin of artistic production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as an organ of human progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is one of two organs of human progress: by words man interchanges thoughts, by the forms of art he interchanges feelings, and this with all men, not only of the present time, but also of the past and the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art by its role in human progress: does it transmit feelings across persons and generations? Art that does not perform this communicative function fails as true art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of feelings (infectiousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art must be capable of infecting others with the same feeling the artist experienced—people must be 'infected by art' to receive it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key test: can the work actually produce in its audience the artist's feeling? If not, it is ineffective. Anti-patterns: works admired for style but unable to move ordinary people are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should unite, not divide, mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Only those productions will be considered art which transmit feelings drawing men together in brotherly union, or such universal feelings as can unite all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer works whose subject-matter and emotional content foster sympathy and social unity. Works that excite exclusive feelings (class-based, nationalistic, or sectarian emotions) are to be judged harmful or unimportant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as necessary spiritual food
rubrics_metrics.description: Select as true art those works which form real, important, necessary spiritual food, and separate them from harmful and useless art and from counterfeits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge works on whether they nourish the spiritual life of individuals and society. If a piece is mere amusement, trivial, or a counterfeit, it should be excluded from this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of counterfeits and trivial/exclusive art
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeits of art (which only serve to amuse and corrupt) and insignificant, exclusive art mistaken for the highest art are not true art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs of deliberate artifice, catering to narrow tastes, or intent to amuse rather than to communicate feeling. Examples cited as counterfeits: spurious popular novels, certain theatre/music/pictures that spread vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral purpose: art should improve goodness
rubrics_metrics.description: True art ought to fertilise and improve people, advancing them towards moral perfection rather than making them coarser or more cruel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work cultivates kindness, compassion, or moral insight. Works that tend to degrade moral sensibilities (e.g., promoting cruelty or vanity) are negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of art that supports an immoral life
rubrics_metrics.description: Art that enables or sanctifies an artificial, idle, or unnatural life (especially of the rich) and conceals its emptiness is harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question whether art is functioning as an opiate for ennui—sustaining lifestyles that contradict humane principles. Anti-pattern: art as entertainment that justifies selfish or luxurious living.

rubrics_metrics.name: No primacy of beauty over goodness
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal of beauty must not supplant the ideal of what is right; putting beauty first frees people from moral demands and can lead to decadence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware aesthetic theories that celebrate beauty for its own sake while denying moral claims. Works that explicitly laud vice or deny moral obligation (decadent/aesthetic movements) should be criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art must not promote superstition, patriotism, or sensuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Art which flourishes in the upper classes has a directly vitiating influence, infecting people with superstition, patriotism, and, above all, sensuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work reinforces ecclesiastical or patriotic superstitions or deliberately inflames sexual desire. Such effects count strongly against it being true art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should not inflame sexual dissoluteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Most art, real and counterfeit, is devoted to describing, depicting, and inflaming sexual love in every shape and form—this tendency is harmful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether sexual depiction serves the transmission of unifying, moral feeling or merely panders to lust and corrupts audiences. Works that sensually titillate without higher purpose are condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public appraisal and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Appraisement of art should devolve to the whole people rather than to a separate class of rich people; art must satisfy demands of the great masses who live in natural conditions of laborious life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works intelligible and emotionally accessible to broad populations. If a piece can only be appreciated by a narrow elite living unnatural conditions, it fails the criterion of universal art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter: feelings accessible to all
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of the future will transmit feelings accessible not only to the rich but to all people—universal feelings that unite everyone without exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess subject-matter for universality: are the feelings depicted commonly shared among ordinary lives (empathy, suffering, compassion)? Avoid elitist preoccupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique defined as clearness, simplicity, and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: In future (true) art the demand will be for clearness, simplicity, and brevity—conditions mastered by education of taste rather than by mechanical exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical execution by clarity and compression rather than by costly, elaborate techniques that serve exclusivity. Anti-pattern: valuing complexity and mannerisms over expressive clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic origin: inner need, not gain
rubrics_metrics.description: The cause of the production of real art is the artist’s inner need to express a feeling; the cause of counterfeit art is gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge authenticity by artistic motivation: was the work produced from deeply felt necessity or engineered for market/success? Works produced mainly for payment/approval are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity vs. artisan repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: A real work of art can only arise in the soul of an artist occasionally; counterfeit art is produced continually by artisans and handicraftsmen if consumers can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for spontaneous, singular creative origin rather than formulaic, mass-produced outputs. Repetitive commercial production is an indicator of counterfeit art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist’s life condition: common life over luxury
rubrics_metrics.description: Security of maintenance and luxury are injurious to an artist’s true productiveness; the artist of the future will live the common life of man, earning subsistence by some labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether an artist’s life keeps them engaged in ordinary human struggle and experience. Extensive luxury/seclusion that removes the artist from common life is detrimental to authentic art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic production: art by the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic activity should be accessible to all; artists will not be merely a few professionals but will include gifted members of the whole people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support institutions and practices that teach basic music and drawing broadly so that talent among the masses can be cultivated. Evaluate whether a culture permits broad participation in art-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique learned in life and example rather than elitist schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Every true artist learns technique chiefly in life, from the examples of the great masters; the loss of professional schools would be compensated by numerous examples of good art among the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the sources of an artist’s technique: preference for experiential learning and readily available exemplars rather than narrowly-gated academies teaches better 'clearness, simplicity, compression.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should reject feelings incompatible with religious perception of brotherhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Art transmitting feelings incompatible with the religious perception of our time—feelings which do not unite but divide men—will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure works against the (broadly defined) religious perception that the aim of life is union of mankind. Works that celebrate division, elitism, or exclusivity fail this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial intermediaries (dealers) degrade the temple of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the dealers are driven out, the temple of art will not be a temple; the art of the future will drive them out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View the role of commercial dealers and gatekeepers skeptically: their presence often furthers counterfeit/exclusive art. Prefer modes of distribution that maximize diffusion and minimize commodification.
